problem.text: The sum of three numbers is $96$. The first number is $6$ times the third number, and the third number is $40$ less than the second number. What is the absolute value of the difference between the first and second numbers?

steps.title: Where to start: name the number everything depends on
steps.body: Both facts describe the other numbers by comparing them to the third number. So call the third number $x$ and write the other two in terms of $x$. Then you only have one unknown. Careful: "the third number is $40$ less than the second" means the second is the bigger one, so the second number is $x+40$, not $x-40$.

your_turn.prompt: Write the first and second numbers in terms of $x$.
your_turn.answer: First is $6x$ (six times the third). Second is $x+40$ (the third is $40$ less than it).

steps.title: Use the sum
steps.body: The three numbers add up to $96$: $$6x + (x+40) + x = 96.$$ Collect the $x$ terms and solve.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: With $x = 7$, the first number is $6\cdot 7 = 42$ and the second is $7+40 = 47$. Check the sum: $42+47+7 = 96$. The difference is $|42-47| = 5$. The answer is **(E)** $5$.

verification.verifier_notes: Passed adversarial verifier on first review.
